subject: Clarify US privacy addendum — service-provider role and transient telemetry (Brightline Health)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Marku s Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Health Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brightline — US privacy addendum/CCPA questions (redline attached)

Hi Markus / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team is reviewing Redwood's DPA and the US privacy addendum. We've attached our redline — a few points are flagged as blockers for execution:

- Whether Redwood will sign up as a "Service Provider" (per CCPA/CPRA) or will want a different processor designation. We need explicit limited-use language.
- Any interstate or cross-border telemetry/operational metrics retention (we need to confirm this data won't be used for marketing or sold).
- Timing and window for subprocessor notice and removal options.

Can you confirm who on Redwood's side will own these items? I attached Brightline_DPA_Redline.docx for your review.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Sr. Contracts Counsel
Brightline Health
[Attachment: Brightline_DPA_Redline.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline — US privacy addendum/CCPA questions (redline attached)

Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear redline.

Quick answers up front so you have them while we pull legal into the thread:
1) Redwood is prepared to be designated a "Service Provider" under CCPA/CPRA with the usual limited-use commitments (no selling, no secondary uses).
2) Telemetry and operational metrics: we currently retain transient telemetry (routing/latency/error rates, aggregated) for debugging and capacity planning. We can propose a 30-day retention window for per-request telemetry and a 90-day aggregated retention in the addendum.
3) Subprocessor notice: standard practice is 30 days' notice before onboarding a new subprocessor, but we can discuss a shorter agreed window for Brightline-critical subprocessors.

I'll loop in Monica from legal to propose specific language and confirm SOC2/KMS controls. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the redline?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marku s Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline — US privacy addendum/CCPA questions (redline attached)

Elena — hi, Monica from Redwood legal. Thanks for the redline; we've reviewed and have proposed language below that aligns with Redwood's operating model. I've attached a marked-up CPRA addendum for convenience (Redwood_CPRA_Addendum_Redline.pdf).

Proposed short-form clause for the addendum (suggestion):
"Redwood acts as a Service Provider/Processor under applicable U.S. state privacy laws (including CCPA/CPRA). Redwood shall process Personal Information only on Customer's documented instructions and for the purpose of providing the Services. Redwood will not sell Personal Information or use Personal Information for any commercial purpose unrelated to providing the Services to Customer. Redwood will implement administrative, technical and physical safeguards consistent with SOC 2 Type II and industry practice. "

On the specific points you flagged:
- Telemetry: Redwood requests a narrow exception permitting transient telemetry and per-request diagnostic data necessary for debugging and SLOs. Proposed limits: per-request identifiers retained up to 30 days, aggregated/metrics retained up to 180 days. PII will be redacted from telemetry by default; any exception would need Customer approval and logging.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current subprocessor registry and notify Brightline at least 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor. For subprocessors handling regulated data, Redwood will provide SOC reports or equivalent on request and will offer to remove or mute a subprocessor for Brightline if a validated risk remediation plan cannot be agreed within 30 days.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood's default data residency is region-aware. For Brightline, we can commit to US-only data residency for production customer data under the DPA; backups and telemetry may be stored in multi-region replicas for disaster recovery, but we can restrict replicas to US regions for this account.

If Brightline can accept the above windowed telemetry approach and the US-only residency for production data, we can provide a clean addendum and a DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
[Attachment: Redwood_CPRA_Addendum_Redline.pdf (pdf)]

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marku s Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Brightline Health Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline — US privacy addendum/CCPA questions (redline attached)

Monica — appreciate the detailed response and suggested language. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) The telemetry windows you propose look closer to what we can accept, but we need a hard commitment that telemetry will not be used for advertising or sold. Please add an explicit prohibition sentence: "Redwood will not use telemetry or operational metrics for advertising, profiling for advertising, or any sale of Personal Information."
2) US-only production residency is critical for Brightline. Please confirm backups and DR replicas can be restricted to US regions only for our tenant.
3) Subprocessor registry + SOC2: please provide the current list and the latest SOC2 Type II report (redacted allowed).

We are willing to proceed quickly if these three items are added to the addendum. I'll also flag two minor redlines in section 4 in our document — attached Brightline_privacy_questions.docx.

Proposed next step: if you can send the updated addendum with those three items by tomorrow morning, we'll route internally and aim to sign next week.

Thanks,
Elena
[Attachment: Brightline_privacy_questions.docx (docx)]

Elena — thanks and appreciate the clear path to close. Summary and commitments from Redwood:

- Non-sale & telemetry prohibition: We will add the explicit prohibition you requested: "Redwood will not use telemetry or operational metrics for advertising, profiling for advertising, or sell Personal Information." That will be in the next redline.
- US-only residency: Confirmed. We will restrict Primary production data and backups/DR replicas to US regions for Brightline's tenant; we'll document the regions in the addendum.
- Subprocessor registry & SOC2: We'll provide a current subprocessor list + a redacted SOC2 Type II report via a secure link. Expect delivery within 48 hours.

Action items and timeline:
1) Monica will produce a clean addendum with the three items and a DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.
2) Ben to schedule a 30-min finalize call with Brightline procurement for Thursday.
3) Redwood to post subprocessor registry and SOC2 link within 48 hours.
